name: pacsci-kit
summary: Rebuilt from the edited generator; footprint, plot, pools and arch positions unchanged. Wall tops are now a flat smooth-quartz parapet with no finials. Every wall's ribs rise and branch into pointed arch heads under a flat white band. Roofs are white, and the five arches are slender one-block frames with a diamond lattice near the crown, lamps on long chains, a flower-shaped fountain bowl and railings on the pool rims.

revisions.comment:
Owner's comment on the Seattle Center render: the surrounding buildings look rough. Fix these on the Pacific Science Center, keeping the footprint, the plot, the pools and the arches' positions, in 1.21.1 blocks:

1. Every wall top is crenellated (merlons all round), so it reads as a castle. Remove all crenellations: Yamasaki's walls end in a clean, flat white parapet.
2. The walls are flat grey with plain pilasters. They should be WHITE (white concrete, smooth quartz, calcite) with Yamasaki's tracery: slender vertical ribs (a block proud, every 3-4 blocks) that rise and branch into tall pointed Gothic arches in the upper third of each wall, and an arcade of pointed arches at the ground floor along the courtyard. Use quartz pillars/walls and stairs to draw the ribs and arch heads.
3. The five lattice arches over the pools are right in place but chunky. Make them slender white pointed arches with open lattice tracery between their two legs (a diamond/rib net near the crown), legs one block thick.
4. The roofs are bare grey. Use a light roofing block (light grey or white concrete, smooth stone) and add the walkways and railings along the pools, the flower-shaped fountain bowl in the main pool, and the lamp globes hanging from the arches.
revisions.summary: Rebuilt from the edited generator; footprint, plot, pools and arch positions unchanged. Wall tops are now a flat smooth-quartz parapet with no finials. Every wall's ribs rise and branch into pointed arch heads under a flat white band. Roofs are white, and the five arches are slender one-block frames with a diamond lattice near the crown, lamps on long chains, a flower-shaped fountain bowl and railings on the pool rims.
applied: 1. No crenellations: the coping is a continuous full smooth_quartz parapet with no quartz_pillar finials (facade.mjs coping). The ribs no longer stick up past it; they end in a flat smooth_quartz band at the parapet line, so every wall top is one flat white line.

2. White tracery walls: ribs stand one block out every 4 cells (corners always ribs) and run up to the upper third. There they branch: upside-down smooth_quartz_stairs shoulders lean on each pair of ribs, with a one-cell pointed slot over each 3-wide panel, under a flat smooth_quartz band (facade.mjs ribs). The ground-floor courtyard arcade of pointed arches stays. Walls that were plain before also got the tracery: the courtyard faces above the promenade, N1's west face, B north east of N1, B' south over the B2 roof, B2's east end and the W stub. Walls on the plot edge (N1 north z0, x0, z177) have the tracery drawn flat in the wall (shell.mjs edgeSkin).

3. Slender arches: parts/arches.mjs rewritten. Each of the two frames per arch is one block thick: a quartz_pillar leg (banded every 6) at each corner on the existing plinths, and smooth_quartz arcs meeting in a point at the crown. In the upper half of the rise there is a diamond net of stepped diagonals, with dangling tips pruned. A smooth_quartz ridge joins the two crowns, and end_rod ties link the frames at the spring. Floating blocks went from 128 to 0.

4. Roof decks are now white_concrete instead of light_gray_concrete. Pool rims along the central N-S and E-W walks have joined diorite_wall railings at y2, with a gap every 8 cells. The NW (main) pool's bowl is now a 7x7 flower (four 3-wide petals plus four diagonal petals, stair lips, a pillar stem with water on top). Each arch has two lantern globes hanging on 8-long chains from the crown ridge.
skipped: Walls on the plot edge (N1's north front at z0, the west edge x0, the tail end z177) can't take ribs that stick out without leaving the plot, so their tracery is drawn flat in the wall (quartz-pillar ribs, calcite lancet strips, quartz heads). It reads more faintly than on the other walls.
Arches keep their two frames each (the plan's grammar). 'Legs one block thick' is done per leg, not by merging each arch into a single frame.
The promenade walkways along the E and S wings were already there and are unchanged; 'walkways along the pools' was met with railings on the existing central walks.
Only the NW (main) pool's fountain bowl became the flower; the SW and SE bowls, which the owner didn't mention, keep their round saucers.
